html:
Comayagua is a town in central Honduras, founded by the Spanish in 1537 and the capital of the colonial province and then of the republic until 1880.

It was chosen for its central place between the two coasts. It became the seat of a bishop, and its cathedral, finished in the early 1700s, holds a clock said to be among the oldest working clocks in the Americas, brought from Spain.

In 1880 President Marco Aurelio Soto moved the capital to Tegucigalpa, the mining town that had become richer and more powerful. Comayagua kept its colonial churches and streets. Under Spanish rule it was part of the Captaincy General of Guatemala, the province from which the Federal Republic of Central America later grew, and its decline mirrors the rise of Honduras's mining interior.
sum: Comayagua is a town in central Honduras, founded by the Spanish in 1537 and the capital of the colonial province and then of the republic until 1880.
